# Wire gyms to the shared mineral kill-drop helper

Implementation task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC1, AC2, AC3).

## Goal

Make every formation gym (including `GymMinerals` and the `GymEnemies` asteroid row) drop minerals on enemy destruction exactly as the game does, by calling the shared helper.

## Minimal implementation

- In `GymFormationScene`, add an injectable RNG (`protected rng: () => number = Math.random` plus a `setRng()`/config seam) used for mineral drops.
- Add a single `_spawnMineralKillDrops(entity)` path that calls `resolveMineralKillDrops(...)` and registers the returned minerals in the gym's mineral field.
- Call it from both the generic destruction path (`onEnemyDestroyed`) and the EXPLODE button (`explodeRandom`), so every destruction path drops exactly once.
- Keep the existing asteroid-split config seam unchanged (splitting stays scene/config-specific).
- Update the `GymMinerals` / `GymFormationScene` docstrings to describe the shared code path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` / `GymEnemies` asteroid row spawns exactly one mineral at its position.
- **AC2 — Gyms re-drop for non-asteroid enemies.** In a gym, a non-asteroid enemy re-drops a configured fraction of the absorbed minerals at its death site.
- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid drop + non-asteroid re-drop) has one production definition that both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` consume.
- Large and medium asteroids drop none directly; their small split children do.
- The gym test suites added by the test-first task pass, and `npm test` plus `npm run typecheck` pass.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `onEnemyDestroyed`, `explodeRandom`, RNG seam, mineral field.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` — docstring/behaviour.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — docstring/behaviour.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` — shared helper (from the previous task).
data.title: Wire gyms to the shared mineral kill-drop helper

# Boss integration on the shared tick (+ teleport avoidance, minions)

**Parent:** `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` (register gap 6). **Depends on:** child #1 (player tick).

## Summary

`PlayScene._updateBoss(dt)` advances the boss inside `tick`, before collisions; `GymBoss.update` calls `super.tick(dt)` and *then* advances the boss, so `GymBoss.tick(dt)` never advances the boss and bullet timing/ordering differs. `PlayScene.getAdditionalTeleportBodies()` makes P7 teleport avoid the boss; `GymBoss` does not. `PlayScene._spawnMinions` spawns phase minions; the gym has no equivalent. Move boss advancement onto the shared tick path (via a hook) and align teleport avoidance and minion spawning.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** — Boss advancement is a shared hook called from `tick`, so a single `tick(dt)` advances the boss in both `PlayScene` and `GymBoss` with the same ordering relative to collisions. Verified by a cross-scene test asserting boss bullets appear after the same `tick`.
- [ ] **AC2** — P7 teleport avoids the boss in `GymBoss` as in the game (shared `getAdditionalTeleportBodies` behaviour).
- [ ] **AC3** — Phase-minion spawning matches the game (or is an explicitly documented, producer-approved constrained-feature difference). If mirrored, `GymBoss` uses the shared `planMinionSpawns`.
- [ ] **AC4** — No observable game change; all `PlayScene` boss tests and `GymBoss` tests pass.
- [ ] **AC5** — All related documentation is updated, including code comments, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3–§5 and the `GymBoss` docstring.
- [ ] **AC6** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.


**Parent-AC traceability** (implements parent `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`):
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC1)** — [ ] **AC1 — Each gap in the register has a single shared implementation.** Gaps 1–11 are closed by extracting the duplicated behaviour into the shared core/module or by consuming an existing shared hook; no production scene re-implements a shared behaviour. Verified by the extended duplicate-body guard and by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC2)** — [ ] **AC2 — Behavioural gaps are closed (or explicitly documented as intentional).** Every behavioural difference identified in gaps 1–11 (P9 magnet in formation gyms, P4 notice, per-type pickup cues, boss-in-`tick`, boss teleport avoidance, teleport gating, hold overflow, restart effect reset, GymPlayer input) is either made identical to the game or recorded as an intentional, approved difference in the epic description and the relevant child.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC3)** — [ ] **AC3 — Cross-scene equivalence for every object.** Automated tests boot both `PlayScene` and each gym and assert identical outcomes for the player, each enemy archetype, asteroids (incl. split), the boss, minerals (collection/hold/choice), power-ups (spawn/lifecycle/collect/magnet/bomb/cues) and projectiles under the same input and `dt`.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC5)** — [ ] **AC5 — No behaviour regression in the game.** `PlayScene` behaviour and all existing tests remain green; any change to game behaviour is called out explicitly in the epic and approved as canonical.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC6)** — [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, the gym docstrings and `README.md` describe the shared behaviour modules, the hooks a gym implements, and the constrained-feature (not divergent-code) nature of gyms.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC7)** — [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** The complete suite (`/skill:test`, `npm test`) passes with zero failures and no newly-flaky tests.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` / `CombatCoreScene.ts` — boss-update hook.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_updateBoss` delegates.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — remove `update` override; implement hooks.
- `src/waves/BossMinions.ts`, `src/entities/Boss.ts` — reused.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.*boss*` — coverage.

## Open questions

- **OQ4 (epic):** should `GymBoss` spawn phase minions as the game does, or is that a deliberately constrained gym feature? *Recommended: mirror it (behaviour), possibly behind a toggle.*
data.title: Boss integration on the shared tick (+ teleport avoidance, minions)

# Level-curve resolver with property tests

## Summary
Implement the pure mathematical module for weapon level curves: diminishing returns, caps, monotonicity, and the level-resolver function that maps (weaponId, level) to per-variable stats.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: Module src/utils/weaponLevels.ts exports a resolveWeaponAtLevel(weaponId, level) function returning per-variable stats.
- AC2: The module defines a WeaponUpgradeSpec type and catalogue covering >= 12 tunable variables (fire rate, projectile count, spread/pattern angle spread, bullet size, bullet speed, lifetime, damage, piercing, bounce, homing strength, AoE radius, status effect chance, chain count, crit multiplier, split-on-hit, knockback force).
- AC3: Each variable uses a diminishing-returns curve (e.g. base * (1 - exp(-k * level)) or similar) with a finite asymptotic cap.
- AC4: Property tests verify monotonic non-decreasing effective values across levels 1..100 for all variables.
- AC5: Property tests verify that no variable exceeds its cap at any level.
- AC6: Property tests verify that the curve is strictly increasing (or constant-at-cap) -- no decreases at higher levels.

## Key Files
- src/utils/weaponLevels.ts (new) -- curve maths, spec catalogue, resolver
- src/utils/weaponLevels.test.ts (new) -- property/unit tests

## Dependencies
- None (pure maths, first in the dependency chain)

## Deliverables
- weaponLevels.ts with WeaponUpgradeSpec, curve functions, resolveWeaponAtLevel
- weaponLevels.test.ts with monotonicity, cap, and resolver tests
- Code comments documenting the curve formula and each variable's behaviour
data.title: Feature: Level-curve resolver with property tests

# Weapon upgrade variable catalogue (>=12 variables)

## Summary
Define the WeaponUpgradeSpec catalogue: enumerate >=12 tunable upgrade variables, specify which >=4 are MVP, document the per-variable curve parameters, and create the type-level contract for level resolution.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: The catalogue documents >=12 tunable upgrade variables across all specified domains (fire rate, projectile count, spread/pattern, size, speed, lifetime, damage, piercing, bounce, homing, AoE, status effects, chain, crit, split, knockback).
- AC2: For each variable, the spec documents: default value, per-level delta/multiplier, cap value, curve type (linear, logarithmic, exponential saturation), and MVP-vs-future classification.
- AC3: MVP variables are >=4 and span multiple behaviour domains (not all from a single category).
- AC4: The spec is documented in code comments within weaponLevels.ts and in GDD section 4.4.
- AC5: The diminishing-returns curve parameters (k, cap) are documented per variable with rationale.

## Key Files
- src/utils/weaponLevels.ts -- WeaponUpgradeSpec catalogue with per-variable metadata
- docs/Game Design Document.md -- section 4.4 update

## Dependencies
- None (runs in parallel with item 1; they share weaponLevels.ts)

## Deliverables
- WeaponUpgradeSpec catalogue in weaponLevels.ts
- GDD 4.4 update
- Per-variable documentation comments

# Per-weapon level state on Player

## Summary
Add per-weapon level tracking to the Player entity: a Map<WeaponId, number> for run-scoped levels, level-up logic on equipWeapon (temporary) and on mineral choice (permanent), level-persistence across weapon timeout, and level-resolved getWeaponDef returning the leveled WeaponDefinition.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: Player tracks a Map<WeaponId, number> for per-weapon run-scoped levels.
- AC2: Collecting a temporary weapon drop (equipWeapon) increments the weapon level and re-activates its timed duration.
- AC3: The level persists for the run even when the weapon times out (weapon stops firing but level is retained; re-collecting re-activates it at the same level).
- AC4: getWeaponDef(id) returns a level-resolved WeaponDefinition (or WeaponLevelStats) incorporating the current level.
- AC5: getWeaponLevel(id) returns the current level for a weapon (defaulting to 0 or 1 for uncollected weapons).
- AC6: resetWeapon() clears timed activations but retains levels (per intake assumption; pending producer confirmation of Reset-drop semantics -- see parent AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J open question).
- AC7: Reset/restart clears all levels (run-scoped).
- AC8: Existing weapon behaviour at level 0/1 is unchanged (no regression).

## Key Files
- src/entities/Player.ts -- _weaponLevels Map, level-up on equipWeapon, level-resolved getWeaponDef, getWeaponLevel
- src/utils/weapons.ts -- extend WeaponDefinition or create WeaponLevelStats interface

## Dependencies
- Level-curve resolver provides resolveWeaponAtLevel

## Deliverables
- Player.ts with _weaponLevels, getWeaponLevel, level-resolved getWeaponDef
- Updated equipWeapon, resetWeapon, resetWeaponTimers
- Back-compat: level 0/1 behaves identically to current unlevelled behaviour
data.title: Feature: Per-weapon level state on Player

# Fire-rate upgrade quantised to beat grid

## Summary
Ensure that fire-rate upgrades from weapon leveling never produce off-grid intervals. Level-resolved fire rates are quantised to valid beat subdivisions, preserving AC6 (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: The level resolver maps fire-rate upgrades to valid beat subdivisions (e.g. 2/beat, 3/beat, 4/beat, 6/beat) -- no arbitrary intervals.
- AC2: The catalogue-wide isOnBeatGrid invariant holds for every weapon at every level (1..100).
- AC3: Property tests verify isOnBeatGrid for all weapons at levels 1..100.
- AC4: If the next subdivision would be off-grid, the system falls back to the nearest valid subdivision.
- AC5: The beat grid test (AH-0MUGY89LE006WVDQ precedent) passes with leveled weapons.

## Key Files
- src/utils/weaponLevels.ts -- fire-rate quantisation in resolveWeaponAtLevel
- src/utils/weapons.ts -- isOnBeatGrid validation at level resolution
- src/utils/weaponLevels.test.ts -- property test: isOnBeatGrid at all levels

## Dependencies
- Level-curve resolver (fire-rate curve + quantisation)

## Deliverables
- Fire-rate quantisation logic in weaponLevels.ts
- isOnBeatGrid property test at all levels
- Updated isOnBeatGrid invariant check in weapons.ts if needed
data.title: Feature: Fire-rate upgrade quantised to beat grid

# Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling

## Summary
Extend the mineral choice system so that when the player has active weapons, the mineral choice offers weapon level-up options alongside the existing power-up choices. Applying a weapon level-up permanently raises that weapon level.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: The mineral choice offers weapon level-up options (leveling an existing weapon by 1) in the pool of available choices.
- AC2: The offered options reflect current weapon levels (higher-level weapons are more attractive offers).
- AC3: Applying a permanent weapon level-up calls Player.equipWeapon(id, true) and increments the weapon permanent level.
- AC4: The mineral choice pool (CHOICE_POOL) is extended with weapon-level-up entries that reference current player weapon levels.
- AC5: If the player has no weapons beyond the cannon, the choice pool falls back to existing behaviour (no weapon-level-up offers).
- AC6: The offer count remains 3 (producer-confirmed 2026-10-02: keep the existing 3-offer mechanism).

## Key Files
- src/powerups/choice.ts -- extend CHOICE_POOL with weapon level-up entries, pluggable strategy
- src/powerups/types.ts -- new choice type for weapon level-up
- src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts -- apply permanent weapon level-up via Player.equipWeapon(id, true)

## Dependencies
- Level-curve resolver, Player level state, pluggable power-up choice strategy (related work AH-0MUCST4M7008O9CX)

## Deliverables
- Extended CHOICE_POOL with weapon level-up options
- New weapon level-up choice type
- mineralLayer.ts to apply permanent level-up
data.title: Feature: Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling

# HUD weapon level readout

## Summary
Display each active weapon level in the HUD so the player can see their weapon progression. One row per active weapon showing weapon name, level, and optionally a visual indicator (e.g. level dots or bar).

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: The HUD displays each active weapon with its current level (e.g. Cannon Lv.3, Spread Lv.2).
- AC2: The level is read from the player level map via player.getWeaponLevel(id).
- AC3: When a weapon levels up, the HUD updates to reflect the new level (reactive update).
- AC4: Weapons at level 0/1 display without a level suffix or with Lv.1 (design decision).
- AC5: Timed weapons show their remaining timer AND their level (two indicators per row).

## Key Files
- src/ui/HUD.ts -- per-weapon level readout
- src/entities/Player.ts -- getWeaponLevel API (from item 3)

## Dependencies
- Player.getWeaponLevel (item 3)

## Deliverables
- HUD.ts with per-weapon level display
- HUD update hook for level-up events
data.title: Feature: HUD weapon level readout

# Weapon-leveling gym demonstration + integration tests

## Summary
Create a dedicated weapon-leveling gym scene (GymWeaponLeveling) that demonstrates temporary leveling (weapon drops) and permanent leveling (mineral choice). Also add integration tests for gym-game parity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: Gym scene GymWeaponLeveling.ts provides an interactive demo where the player can collect weapon drops to level up weapons and use mineral choices for permanent leveling.
- AC2: The gym demonstrates all >=4 MVP upgrade variables changing visibly at higher levels.
- AC3: The HUD in the gym shows per-weapon levels.
- AC4: The gym is registered in the gym index (consistent with existing gym discovery pattern).
- AC5: Integration tests verify weapon-drop leveling and permanent-choice leveling work end-to-end.
- AC6: Gym-game parity tests (duplicate-body/equivalence guard) pass for leveled weapons.

## Key Files
- src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts (new) -- demonstration gym scene
- src/scenes/gym/index.ts -- register new gym
- src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.weaponLevels.test.ts -- integration tests
- src/scenes/__tests__/GymParity.test.ts -- gym-game parity

## Dependencies
- Shared core leveled effects (item 4), HUD level readout (item 7), mineral-choice leveling (item 6)

## Deliverables
- GymWeaponLeveling.ts gym scene
- Gym index registration
- Integration tests
- Parity tests
